Context: None

Question: "A friend of yours says, “Every time I plan a vacation, there's always a crisis at home or work so that I can't go."" Assuming that this is not really true, your friend's statement best illustrates which of the following?"

Options: 
A. illusory correlation
B. base rate fallacy
C. cognitive dissonance
D. anchoring bias
E. availability heuristic
F. fundamental attribution bias
G. hindsight bias
H. self-serving bias
I. psychological reactance
J. confirmation bias

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.

The crises are memorable, so the friend thinks they happen "every time", even though statistically (based on the "user's assumption that this is not really true" logic), they don't happen enough to be "always". While similar, the Availability Heuristic is the more direct fit for "memory availability leads to frequency misestimation".

That's usually "You are a cool guy so you always succeed" (Stereotype) or noticing coincidences between unrelated events (e.g., "I wear these shoes, then I always win at work"). While there is a correlation (vacation planning -> crisis), the prompt focuses on the *frequency* claim ("always" vs "not really true").
    *   Conclusion: **Availability heuristic** (E) is the strongest candidate.
